entries.title: Five states join FTC amended complaint against Hims and Hers over subscription billing, cancellation and privacy practices
entries.facts: In a press release dated November 10, 2026, the Federal Trade Commission states that an amended complaint in its action against Hims and Hers was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, and that the amended complaint alleges Hims has violated Arizona, Florida, Nebraska, Ohio and Wisconsin state consumer protection laws in addition to the FTC Act, the Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act and California and Utah consumer protection laws. On the billing allegations the release states that the company fails to clearly disclose that it charges consumers for prescriptions almost immediately after they submit an intake form, and that it has made it difficult for consumers to cancel subscriptions. The release separately alleges that the company shared consumers' health information with Meta, Snap and other third parties. The five joining states are Arizona, Florida, Nebraska, Ohio and Wisconsin, in addition to Utah and California, the latter by and through Los Angeles County Counsel. The underlying amended complaint was not retrieved; the source of record is the Commission's own announcement.
entries.relevant_to: subscription billers, payment processors, direct-to-consumer and telehealth platforms

entries.title: California joins two bipartisan multistate amicus briefs backing New York and Wisconsin against Kalshi on gambling-law preemption
entries.facts: In a press release dated November 6, 2026, the California Department of Justice states that Attorney General Rob Bonta joined two bipartisan coalitions of attorneys general in filing two amicus briefs supporting New York's and Wisconsin's right to enforce state sports gaming and gambling laws against prediction market operator Kalshi, and describes these as the tenth and eleventh times California has joined such multistate efforts. The release states that the attorneys general primarily argue that federal preemption of state gambling laws as applied to prediction market providers is improper. On the New York matter, the release states that in KalshiEX, LLC v. Williams, et al. the district court denied Kalshi's preliminary injunction motion, holding that New York gambling laws as applied to Kalshi's sports-event contracts are not preempted, and that Kalshi has appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit. On the Wisconsin matter, the release states that Wisconsin filed a state-court action against Coinbase, Kalshi, Robinhood, Polymarket and Crypto.com, that after removal to federal court the Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed its own federal suit against Wisconsin with a preliminary injunction motion to block enforcement of the state's gambling laws, that the district court denied that motion, and that the CFTC has appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit. The release links a Second Circuit and a Seventh Circuit amicus brief; neither brief was retrieved. No docket numbers or hearing dates are stated.
entries.source_label: California Attorney General press release, November 6, 2026

entries.title: Michigan Gaming Control Board marks Illegal Gambling Awareness Week, naming unlicensed sweepstakes casinos and prediction markets
entries.facts: In a release datelined Detroit, November 10, 2026, the Michigan Gaming Control Board announces its participation in Illegal Gambling Awareness Week alongside international regulators, under the message Play It Safe. Bet Legal. The release states that illegal operators, including offshore websites, unlicensed sweepstakes casinos, and prediction markets offering sports contracts without a Michigan license, are not subject to the rules that apply to licensed operators; advises consumers to be wary of sites that accept cryptocurrency only; states that licensed operators must meet requirements including protecting player funds and personal information using secure payment methods; and states that the Board has sent hundreds of cease-and-desist letters to unlicensed operators. The release also recaps three earlier matters: a preliminary injunction barring Kalshi from offering sports event contracts to people in Michigan, secured in September; an October agreement under which Coinbase agreed to stop offering sports-related event contracts, including those traded on Kalshi, to Michigan customers; and a federal court-approved agreement dated October 28 under which Polymarket US agreed to stop offering new sports-related event contracts in Michigan and to close any open contracts held by Michigan residents by November 25. The release announces no new enforcement action, order, rule or licensing action of its own.
entries.source_label: Michigan Gaming Control Board press release, November 10, 2026
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sweepstakes casinos, online gaming operators
